name: Revolutionary socialism
summary: Revolutionary socialism holds that capitalism cannot be reformed into socialism and that the working class must take political power through social revolution, ending private ownership of the means of production and eventually classes and the state. It is defined against reformist social democracy, and covers a family running from orthodox Marxism and Luxemburg to Lenin's vanguard party and Trotsky. Violence is not essential to the definition, but the seizure of power is.
scope: The Marxist-rooted mainstream of the family: Marx and Engels's Communist Manifesto, Luxemburg's Reform or Revolution and Lenin's State and Revolution and wartime writings. It does not cover anarchist or syndicalist currents, nor Stalinist or Maoist specifics; questions on which Leninist and Luxemburgist strands disagree (single-party rule, vanguard, civil liberties) are answered 0 or as split.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Free public services are a standard demand in the Manifesto's programme and revolutionary socialists want health care guaranteed as a social right.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Revolutionary socialists back higher pay as a fight within capitalism but see wage labour itself as the problem, so support is lukewarm and inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Manifesto and its heirs hold that production for the market under private capital must be replaced, not praised for efficiency.

public-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto calls for centralising production and key sectors such as transport and communications in the hands of the state after the workers win power.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Manifesto lists a heavy progressive income tax as an early measure, though as a stepping stone, not the goal.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are seen as schools of class organisation, though revolutionary socialists criticise union leaders who accept capitalism.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Manifesto's central claim is that bourgeois private property must be abolished and requires despotic inroads upon property rights.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Revolutionary socialists regard regulation as a reformist half-measure that leaves capital in place, though they would not oppose it; adherents are split on its worth.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare is a gain won by working-class pressure, and cutting it is opposed as an attack on workers even if reforms do not end exploitation.

worker-ownership.rationale: The goal is common ownership of the means of production by the associated producers, which workers' collective control of firms expresses.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed directly; revolutionary movements have long been targets of state surveillance and distrust the capitalist state's security apparatus.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Classical sources are silent and modern revolutionary socialists are divided between libertarian and puritanical attitudes.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents split between support for banning fascist propaganda and wariness of giving the capitalist state censorship powers.

strong-leader.rationale: Luxemburg stresses the conscious mass movement over rule by individuals, and the tradition treats emancipation as the act of the working class itself.

state-harmful.rationale: The state is seen as an instrument of class rule that must be seized or smashed and eventually withers, but a workers' state is wanted for the transition, so it is not simply harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Lenin wants the people armed in a militia, but modern adherents are divided over civilian gun control.

empower-police-military.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution calls for breaking up the standing army and police of the bourgeois state, so they oppose strengthening them.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not a defining question; socialists split between seeing sex work as exploitation to abolish and as work to decriminalise.

decide-locally.rationale: Lenin's workers' state is centralised but built from local councils, so adherents do not take a clear side on localism.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the view that crime stems from social conditions, not innate nature.

traditional-family.rationale: The Manifesto predicts the bourgeois family will vanish with capital and treats it as resting on private gain.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not in the classical texts; modern revolutionary socialist organisations generally support LGBT rights.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's support for women's emancipation and the usual stance of modern socialist organisations.

more-religion-public.rationale: Marx treats religion as a response to alienation that fades with material emancipation, so a bigger public role for it runs against the programme.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's opposition to oppression and its view that racism divides the working class, though adherents stress class over race.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Marx holds that human nature and social forms are historically made, from which adherents usually infer a constructed view of gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Manifesto says the working men have no country and national divisions are already fading, so preserving national tradition is not a priority.

gradual-change.rationale: Luxemburg argues reforms only operate within the framework the last revolution made and that the working class must conquer political power, not wait for gradual change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Workers of all countries are held to share one class interest, so adherents oppose restricting immigration as dividing workers.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Internationalism means solidarity among workers across borders, not strengthening bodies of capitalist states such as the UN.

free-trade.rationale: The Manifesto sees the world market as creating a global proletariat but not as benefiting everyone; free trade is seen as serving capital.

nation-first.rationale: Lenin rejects defence of the fatherland in imperialist war and puts international working-class interest first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from hostility to imperialist wars led by capitalist powers, which adherents suspect of cloaking their own interests.

open-borders.rationale: With the proletariat having no country and national barriers vanishing, they favour open borders, though few make it a demand for the present.

limit-growth.rationale: Marxist tradition favours developing productive forces for need, though eco-socialist currents dissent; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Modern revolutionary socialists blame capitalist production for climate change and call for drastic action, but classical texts are silent.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Marx sees technology as raising productive forces but insists social relations decide who benefits, so adherents are split on this claim.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; modern adherents divide between pro-nuclear and ecological positions.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Manifesto openly declares that ends can be attained only by the forcible overthrow of all existing social conditions, and revolution is the defining belief of the tradition.

experts-over-public.rationale: Lenin holds that any literate worker can manage accounting and control, and Marx praised the Commune's democracy without professionals.

central-planning.rationale: The Manifesto envisions centralising production in the hands of the state, but later revolutionary socialists differ about how centralised planning should be.

socialized-markets.rationale: Revolutionary socialists mostly aim at abolishing commodity production, though some accept markets during transition; adherents are divided.

land-value-tax.rationale: A land tax does not abolish property, and the Manifesto wants rents applied to public purposes within a wider programme, not a single tax that replaces others.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The Manifesto lists the abolition of all right of inheritance among its measures, so heavy taxation is a milder version they would endorse.

basic-income.rationale: Seen by some as a useful reform and by others as a reformist palliative that leaves wage labour intact.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and from seeing tariffs as favouring national capitalists rather than workers.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Centralised credit and state-directed production are part of the Manifesto programme for the transition.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Manifesto criticises small property as already being destroyed by industry and wants common ownership, not spread-out small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Manifesto condemns wage labour, and Lenin projects a higher phase beyond bourgeois law, but timing is held unknowable.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The Manifesto calls for centralising credit in a national bank under state control, the opposite of abolishing it for market money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Class collaboration through state-recognised bodies is rejected as a reformist or fascist substitute for class struggle.

one-party-rule.rationale: Leninist strands defend vanguard party rule, while Luxemburgist, council and Trotskyist-democratic strands insist on pluralism within soviet democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Manifesto treats ruling-class property and privilege as what the proletariat must overthrow, and hereditary monarchy is a clear case of ruling-class rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Luxemburg calls democracy necessary and indispensable to the working class, though revolutionary socialists criticise bourgeois democracy as limited.

direct-votes.rationale: Lenin and Marx praise direct popular participation in a commune-style state, but referendum rule is not a stated programme.

workers-councils.rationale: Soviets and workers' councils are cited as the organs of working-class power in the revolutionary tradition, notably Luxemburgist and Leninist.

right-to-secede.rationale: Lenin defended the right of nations to self-determination including separation, as part of struggle against oppression.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Manifesto holds that ruling ideas are those of the ruling class, rejecting the notion that anyone is born to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Manifesto states ends can be attained only by forcible overthrow, so adherents reject the view that political violence is never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Lenin condemns imperialist war as a reactionary war of capitalist states and calls for turning it into civil war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Marx and later revolutionary socialists demand the separation of religion and state, with religion a private matter.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religion is treated as an ideology reflecting alienation, so scriptural law is rejected.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state's functions in defence and justice are held to belong to society as a whole, not companies seeking profit.

military-superiority.rationale: Revolutionary socialists oppose arms races between capitalist powers and the military machinery of the state.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Manifesto says the working men have no country and national differences are vanishing, which rules out ethnic nationhood as a goal.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Manifesto opens by stating that the history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Lenin holds that equal pay for labour is only the first phase, and the end goal of need-based distribution is a deeper equality, but not simple equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from support for anti-colonial self-determination, though classical texts do not address it.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism; Lenin condemns colonial oppression though reparations are not a classic demand.

civilizational-union.rationale: Unity is held to be of the working class across all countries, not along religion or civilisation.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The tradition condemns the egoistic calculation of bourgeois society and holds free development of each to depend on that of all.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Manifesto's association where each's free development is the condition of all's is neither duty over rights nor the reverse; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Marx stresses the metabolism of humans and nature, but valuing nature in itself is a modern ecosocialist addition on which adherents differ.

limit-population.rationale: Marxists traditionally blame poverty on social relations, not population growth, so coercive limits are disfavoured; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Marxism praises capitalism for raising productive forces and wants to take them over, not reject industry.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not a position of the tradition; the Manifesto values growth of productive forces but social ownership is the concern.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed and adherents have no common view.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Lenin wants administration by the armed people and simple accounting, not rule by technocratic systems; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from distrust of the capitalist state's surveillance of revolutionary movements.

restore-past-order.rationale: The Manifesto presents bourgeois society's sweeping away of old orders as a progressive step and looks forward, not back.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The tradition holds that policy serves class interests and a theory of history, so it rejects judging apart from ideology.

direct-action.rationale: Luxemburg values mass action and the party contests elections as a school for workers, so adherents use both, with seizure of power the aim.

means-match-ends.rationale: Leninists accept dictatorial means during transition while Luxemburgists stress democratic means; the tradition is split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The Manifesto praises the development of productive forces and aims to take over industry, not abandon it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Lenin quotes the vision of the vanishing of the difference between mental and physical labour in the higher phase, as a long-term aim.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution states the higher phase's principle: from each according to ability, to each according to needs.

production-for-use.rationale: The Manifesto condemns production for private profit and capital that lives only by exploiting labour, favouring production for social needs.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Manifesto states that wage labour produces capital which exploits wage labour, with wages reduced to bare subsistence.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Lenin describes the proletarian dictatorship as the majority suppressing the former exploiters, though libertarian strands object to the term.

collective-farming.rationale: The Manifesto calls for cultivation under a common plan but later revolutionary socialists disagree about peasant collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Lenin treats the war of 1914 as an imperialist war of capitalist powers; adherents of Luxemburg's and Lenin's circle say the same.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Manifesto explicitly proposes a heavy progressive income tax as a revolutionary measure.

harm-principle.rationale: Not a framing the tradition uses; adherents accept restrictions on exploiters while supporting freedoms for workers.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Marx criticised bourgeois rights as those of an egoistic individual, and the tradition values collective class action; inferred.

conscription.rationale: Lenin's militia of the whole people is mandatory in spirit, but adherents oppose conscription into capitalist armies.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The tradition wants collective political power for the working class, not individual exit.

state-as-business.rationale: The Manifesto holds that the bourgeois state is a committee for managing the common affairs of the bourgeoisie, not a model to copy.

positive-liberty.rationale: The Manifesto's aim of an association where each can develop freely requires the material means, which capitalism denies to workers.

media-academia-power.rationale: Ruling ideas are held to be those of the economic ruling class, so capital, not intellectuals, holds the real power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The tradition treats human difference as social and historical, and revolutionary organisations oppose racial science.

organic-representation.rationale: Estates and trade-body representation is a corporatist idea; revolutionary socialists favour class-based councils or party mass politics.

total-state.rationale: Lenin's state is meant to wither and administration to be taken over by the people, though Leninist strands accept strong control in transition.

national-rebirth.rationale: Nationalist rebirth is alien to a project aimed at class emancipation across countries.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Lenin condemns imperialist war of aggression as reactionary and calls for working-class defeatism toward such wars.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The Manifesto presents feudal bonds as having been swept away and rejects rule built on personal loyalty.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom and bondage are described in the Manifesto as old forms of exploitation that the proletarian movement opposes.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The Manifesto holds ruling ideas to be the ruling class's, but Marxism also claims scientific status for itself, so adherents are cautious.

universal-morality.rationale: SEP notes that Marx regards morality as ideology tied to class interests, though debate continues.

single-common-good.rationale: The Manifesto treats society as split into classes with opposed interests, so there is no single common good in class society.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's critique of nationalism and defence of the Bund and diaspora struggle; adherents split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of ethnic nationhood and national exclusivism.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not a concern of a tradition that treats national differences as secondary to class.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Revolutionary socialist strands such as council communism and soviet theory describe workers controlling production through councils.

school-vouchers.rationale: The Manifesto calls for free public education for all children, not private choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not a concern of the tradition, which sees deficit orthodoxy as capital's austerity; inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: The tradition regards economic freedom of capital as the freedom to exploit, not as a basis for political freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rule is analysed in terms of class power and institutions, not the virtue of rulers.

national-self-determination.rationale: Lenin defended nations' right to self-government as part of the democratic struggle against oppression.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred from opposition to imperialist wars regardless of whether the UN approves.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Marx calls religion an illusion and claims a scientific basis for socialism, but adherents do not claim reason is the only guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The working class is one across borders, so welfare restricted by citizenship is rejected as dividing workers.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Compulsory work for benefits is seen as coercion of the poor under capitalism.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Manifesto's core claim is of opposed classes locked in struggle, and revolutionary socialists reject class cooperation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Marx's tradition wants to take over and use the cultural inheritance of humanity, not destroy it; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Lenin supported anti-imperialist movements but adherents are wary of fronts with non-socialist rulers.

workers-nation.rationale: The Manifesto proclaims the working men have no country and calls for united action of workers of several countries.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Manifesto criticises the bourgeois treatment of women as instruments of production and calls for ending it.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury is condemned by some but the tradition targets capital as such, not interest alone.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The tradition holds that racial division splits the working class and opposes laws enforcing it, in line with its call for the unity of workers of all countries.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Manifesto defines political power as the organised power of one class for oppressing another and the state as the bourgeoisie's managing committee.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from modern revolutionary socialists' climate stance; classical texts silent.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Workers of all countries are one class and demanding assimilation is nationalist; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy of replacement is alien to a class analysis; the Manifesto explains migration by capital's search for cheap labour and unity of workers.

proportional-representation.rationale: Luxemburg values democracy but revolutionary socialists treat electoral systems as secondary to the conquest of power.

national-mission.rationale: Lenin condemns the great powers' imperialist missions and calls for the fraternal union of workers instead.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Manifesto sees the bourgeois family and women's position as rooted in property relations, which modern adherents extend into a structural analysis.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Luxemburg calls bourgeois parliamentarism a display of class antagonisms, and revolutionary socialists see politicians as serving capital.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy is rejected by the tradition, which attributes social ills to class relations.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Lenin wants the standing police broken up, but accountability for past abuses is not a classic topic; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Manifesto's programme assigns the state active economic roles after the revolution; a minimal state protecting property is the opposite of its aim.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racial division is treated as a device that divides the working class, and the tradition rejects racial hierarchy.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Manifesto's final vision is an association where free development of each is the condition for all.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Lenin and Trotsky hold that the revolution must spread internationally, while Stalinist strands accept socialism in one country; the family is split.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Revolutionary socialists differ and the classical texts say little.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from secularism and equality before the law, though adherents are cautious about minority rights.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religion is treated as a private matter and coercive restriction is rejected, though Marx dismisses it as illusion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religiously motivated ban is rejected by a tradition that treats religion as ideology.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Manifesto wants education freed from ruling-class influence, and the tradition demands secular state schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Leninist strands defend a strong state under encirclement, while Luxemburgist ones argue the dictatorship must remain democratic; adherents split.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Luxemburg's conquest of power by the conscious popular mass rests on mass support, but the tradition does not accept consent as bourgeois legitimacy.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist national aims are alien to an internationalist outlook; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Lenin's internationalism and defence of oppressed nations oppose forcing out minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Manifesto endorses forcible overthrow and despotic inroads on property, directly contradicting the non-initiation principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The Manifesto holds that class struggle drives history, and condemns capitalist competition, not praises it as progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Luxemburg values democratic liberties as indispensable to the working class, and revolutionary parties are themselves targets of such bans.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's critique of capitalist domination over workers' lives.

separated-powers.rationale: Lenin and Marx praise the Commune as a working body combining executive and legislative functions.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Wikipedia article notes Leninist strands favour a vanguard party while Luxemburgists criticise it for underrating spontaneity, so the family is genuinely split.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The working class is the class the whole programme serves, so they would give its needs priority.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Seen as privatisation eroding social housing; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes are weapons of class struggle and the tradition opposes legal restriction of them.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The Manifesto and Marx place poverty in exploitation under capitalism, not in the number of people.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The tradition holds that class, not ethnicity, is the main division in society.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Lenin and Marx favour recall and rotation of officials but lotteries are not part of the tradition.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Leninist strands accept emergency measures against counter-revolution, while Luxemburgists stress liberties, so adherents split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from support for state intervention to protect workers in scarcity.

party-controls-media.rationale: Luxemburg defends freedom of expression and criticised bureaucratic suppression, though Leninist strands accept censorship.

party-commands-army.rationale: Leninists favour party control of the army while Luxemburgists and others favour an armed people; split.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship barriers divide workers, so the tradition would oppose them.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution, following Marx on the Commune, demands that officials be paid workmen's wages.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Leninist tradition holds that members carry out decisions once adopted, though Luxemburgist strands are wary of centralism.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The EU is seen as a capitalist bloc, though the tradition favours a socialist union of peoples.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Lenin wants the standing army and bureaucracy broken up and replaced by an armed people, not commanded by a head of state.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Religion is treated as a private matter and hierarchical churches get no support.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by clergy is incompatible with the tradition's secularism and class-based democratic power.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Lenin states a revolutionary class cannot but desire the defeat of its own government in a reactionary war and rejects neither victory nor defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moral censorship is seen as bourgeois; Stalinist strands differ.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed, though recall of officials is favoured; adherents have no common view.

recall-officials.rationale: Lenin follows Marx's Commune in making officials subject to recall at any time.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Revolutionary socialists oppose imperialist alliances and military blocs of capitalist states.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The Manifesto wants rents applied to public purposes, not a ban on renting by individuals; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Lenin calls for replacing the standing army with the armed people organised as a militia.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Manifesto speaks of rescuing a considerable part of the population from the idiocy of rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is not a classic aim; adherents differ.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Revolutionary socialists accept intellectuals joining the movement, so are not hostile to the educated in general; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred from rejection of civilizational hierarchy, but the Manifesto also ranks stages of production.

death-penalty.rationale: Many revolutionary socialists oppose capital punishment, though Leninist practice made exceptions.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's support for women's equality and free public education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Religious doctrine in science teaching is rejected by a tradition that sees religion as illusion.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Socialists differ between moral and libertarian positions.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Descent-based citizenship rests on national exclusivity, which the tradition rejects.

minority-language-support.rationale: Lenin defended equality of nations and languages against national oppression.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious freedom is accepted as private but exemptions from general laws are not addressed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The tradition values free development but this is not a defining position.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-imperialist strands call for cancelling debts that bind poor countries to rich ones; inferred from anti-imperialism.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Lenin's view that formal national freedom within capitalism leaves economic dependence in place.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Luxemburg supported a constituent assembly while Leninists dissolved it in favour of soviets; split.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Luxemburg held that democratic liberties are indispensable, though Leninist strands accept limits.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Aid is seen as charity within imperialism; socialists would rather see transformation of the system.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Revolutionary socialists oppose capitalist states' arms races.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The Manifesto wants credit centralised under the state, not left to independent bankers.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Revolutionary socialists criticise territorial nationalism and favour peace settlements; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The Manifesto goes further and abolishes bourgeois property, so a mild common-good limit is a step short of their position.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Trotskyists and left communists call the USSR a degenerated workers' state or state capitalist, while Leninist strands call it socialist, so the family is divided.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common view.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliances like NATO are seen as capitalist blocs of imperialist war.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from Lenin's defence of the right of oppressed nations to self-determination.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The tradition wants church property and power curbed and religion made a private matter.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A symbolic unifying head of state is a bourgeois device that hides class division.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Lenin upheld the right of nations to secede, so adherents do not favour force to prevent it.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; adherents differ.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Sacred, divinely descended rule is a clear case of old ruling ideology the Manifesto opposes.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The Manifesto lists a heavy progressive income tax among its measures.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marx's view that ideas and consciousness are shaped by material conditions supports this.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Lenin wants the state accountable to the armed people, not a ruler above laws.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common view.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Class-based rule is to be ended, not balanced between few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Luxemburg's emphasis on conscious mass movement is against leader worship, though Stalinist strands differ.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common view.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Maoists hold this, Trotskyists warn of bureaucratic restoration, but others deny it, so adherents split.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Manifesto's measures include abolishing property in land, and redistribution to cultivators is a standard peasant demand though they prefer common ownership.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and opposition to expulsions of peoples.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Territorial claims on grounds of nationality are nationalist, and the Manifesto says the working men have no country.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Religion is treated as a private matter, and punishing leaving it is incompatible with that.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory dress codes for women conflict with the tradition's call to end women's subordination.

common-currency.rationale: Revolutionary socialists criticise the euro as a capitalist project but not on the currency principle alone.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Unity is sought across the working class, not along language families and ancestry.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Lenin opposed national cultural autonomy while the Bund and Austrian Marxists proposed it, so the tradition is split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Lenin and Luxemburg backed minorities fighting for equal rights where they live and joining the common class struggle.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: SEP presents Marx's view that historical change follows development of productive forces that fetter existing economic structures.

ban-cartels.rationale: Concentration of capital is seen as a tendency of capitalism that prepares socialisation, not something to break up for competition.

no-bailouts.rationale: Adherents dislike bailouts of capital but also favour state ownership of failed banks; split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Revolutionary socialists treat bourgeois courts as class institutions but also value democratic liberties; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from support for women's equality in modern revolutionary organisations.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The Manifesto sees the world market as global and favours united action across countries, not colonial blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Revolutionary socialists regard such clauses as reformist, but not opposed.

moral-incentives.rationale: Lenin sees labour becoming a prime want only in the higher phase while the first phase pays by labour done, so adherents differ.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Luxemburg contrasts Blanqui's coups by an active minority with conquest of power by a conscious popular mass.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Manifesto's measures include abolishing the right of inheritance and the tradition opposes aristocratic privilege.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Lenin condemns imperialist rule over colonies as oppression.

patriotic-education.rationale: Lenin rejects defence of the fatherland and teaching national pride is nationalist.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from support for correcting racial injustice.

public-money-creation.rationale: The Manifesto calls for centralising credit in a state national bank.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Luxemburg argued against Bernstein's belief that capitalism adapts and avoids collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Imperial influence is rejected by anti-imperialist revolutionaries.

delink-world-market.rationale: Lenin sought socialist revolution in advanced countries more than delinking, and adherents are split.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Lenin argued that bribed upper strata of workers exist, but others hold that the working class in rich countries is still exploited; split.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's opposition to oppression and unlimited property rights.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Luxemburg valued democratic rights, but the tradition mistrusts entrenching bourgeois legal limits; split.

elective-rulers.rationale: Lenin and Marx want all officials elected and recallable, as in the Commune.

minority-veto.rationale: Marxist tradition holds that the majority decides and suppresses the exploiters, not that minorities can veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's right of revolution against the ruling class.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Luxemburg values parliament as a platform but rejects it as the means of transition and Lenin wanted to replace it with soviets.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common view.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common view.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The tradition rejects charity from the privileged and calls for abolition of class privilege.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The tradition calls for active class struggle and the conquest of political power.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The Manifesto says the ruling ideas are those of the ruling class, but the tradition also stresses that workers can break from them.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The Manifesto's view of ruling ideas implies consent shapes rule, but revolutionary socialists emphasise force and the state too.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Lenin's imperialism analysis holds that colonial powers extract surplus from dependent countries.

native-born-offices.rationale: Workers have no country, so reserving offices for native-born citizens is rejected.

party-own-road.rationale: Trotskyists and Luxemburgists reject directions from a foreign party while Comintern-style strands accepted it; split.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not a defining position; adherents differ.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Territorial revanchism is nationalist and conflicts with internationalism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of ethnic hierarchy though the tradition backs anti-colonial struggles.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from opposition to fascism, though adherents also criticise liberal constitutions.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Revolutionary socialists reject equating fascism with communism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Marxists treat the war as class and property conflict over slave labour.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from a view of history as class struggle that does not honour rulers.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not a position of the tradition; adherents differ.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Adherents differ and the tradition treats gender violence as structural.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Revolutionary socialists do not hold civilizational relativism of institutions but accept different paths.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Lenin wants the standing army broken up and replaced by the armed people, not made a political guardian.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's concern for ending the treatment of women as instruments of production and from socialist feminism.

filial-duty.rationale: The Manifesto sees family bonds as resting on capital and expected to fade; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Lenin wants officials elected, recallable and paid workmen's wages, not a professional class chosen by examination.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Revolutionary socialists want expropriation not national protection, adherents differ.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's critique of the bourgeois family.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Lenin sets out officials subject to recall at any time, following the Commune.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Privatising social insurance contradicts the programme of common provision and ending capital's claim on workers.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Manifesto calls for abolishing property in land, and use-based tenure is consistent, though not a stated programme.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Luxemburg values parliament as a stage but adherents have no stated view on budget powers.

single-official-language.rationale: Lenin opposed compulsory state language and defended equality of languages.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and from the aim of ending private property in land anyway.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The tradition criticises capitalist production for profit and false needs, and wants production for need.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Revolutionary socialists support insurgent struggles but not state policy of capitalist countries.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Luxemburg defended the self-determination of peoples, so Soviet-style interventions are opposed by Luxemburgists and Trotskyists, but not by all Leninists.

corporate-influence.rationale: The state is seen as a committee of the bourgeoisie, so corporate influence is a reflection of capital's rule.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from defence of civil liberties of the working class and distrust of state power.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not a position of the tradition, which opposes nationalist population policy.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Manifesto calls for equal liability of all to labour, and socialists favour full employment under public ownership.

democratic-peace.rationale: Lenin treats imperialist war as arising from capitalism, including among democracies.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The tradition treats law as expression of ruling-class interest, so obedience to it is not a moral duty.

non-intervention.rationale: Revolutionary socialists favour international solidarity but oppose imperialist interventions.

industrial-unions.rationale: Revolutionary syndicalists and many Marxists favour industrial unionism, though craft unions exist.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy beliefs against minorities contradict a class analysis of society.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marxists criticise bourgeois marriage, but whether to abolish its legal form divides adherents.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Lenin sees administration as simple enough for all to take part and control, which requires access to information.

local-production.rationale: The Manifesto welcomes the world market's development and sees socialism as global.

informal-organisation.rationale: Lenin's and Luxemburg's traditions build mass parties and councils, not informal affinity groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Internationalism mistrusts national precedence, but international courts are bourgeois too; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: National community defined by religion is rejected given the workers have no country.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Lenin condemns imperial dominance and tribute relations.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from solidarity across regions and class.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Manifesto says Communists do not abolish personal property earned by one's own labour, only bourgeois property in capital.

defeat-communism.rationale: Communism is the movement's own aim.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Private provision for profit contradicts the aim of public ownership.

religion-illusion.rationale: SEP notes Marx sees religion as a response to material alienation that should fade once material life is emancipated.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Manifesto praises the bourgeoisie for creating immense productive forces and shaping the world market.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Manifesto ties the bourgeois family and women's status to capital and expects change with its abolition.

socialized-care.rationale: The Manifesto's social education and the tradition's view of domestic labour support socialising it.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic nationalism is alien to internationalism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed; Lenin defended national self-determination, but the status of treaties with internal nations is not a stated position and adherents differ.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The Manifesto criticises utopian small communities and wants class struggle and state power instead.

majority-settlement.rationale: Settling majority groups in minority regions is national oppression that Lenin opposed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Communism is the aim, so a third course is rejected.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of nationalist territorial claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Holocaust denial is rejected by all revolutionary socialist organisations, which oppose fascism and antisemitism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Modern revolutionary socialist organisations oppose criminalisation, though some historical regimes did it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Luxemburg held that democratic liberties are indispensable to the workers, though Leninist strands accept repression of exploiters.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The tradition separates religion from state and regards religion as private.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Lenin condemns colonial exploitation as imperialism.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred from secularism, though socialists support anti-colonial resistance.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Religious legitimacy of rule is rejected by the tradition's secular materialism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Lenin and Marx praise the Commune where ordinary people take direct part in administration.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The Manifesto links class and family oppression, and modern adherents extend this, though some stress class primacy.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Modern revolutionary socialist organisations generally support trans rights, but the classical texts do not address it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The class-struggle tradition sees opposed class interests, so combining left and right is rejected.

alienated-labor.rationale: SEP describes Marx's alienation: labour under capitalism separates workers from the product, activity, others and human nature.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Revolutionary socialists reject cultural essentialism and see workers of all religions as one class.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority from God is rejected since religion is held to reflect alienation.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: French-style laicist and civil libertarian strands both exist on the left, so adherents split.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from support for workers against employers.

social-market-economy.rationale: This is the social-democratic reformism that revolutionary socialists oppose.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Lenin wants the standing army replaced by an armed people, and abolition of standing armies is a goal, but a workers' state needs defence; split.

rich-first.rationale: The tradition rejects letting capitalists grow rich while workers follow.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Lenin refused to back either imperialist camp, but adherents differ about neutrality in modern blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary office is a feudal remnant that Marxists reject, and revolutionary socialists want classless, stateless self-rule.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The Manifesto demands centralising credit in a state bank; mutualist user-owned banks are a Proudhonian idea the family rejects as reformist, but some adherents would accept them as a step.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and opposition to finance capital; the sources discuss neither the IMF nor debt, and revolutionaries see refusal as insufficient without breaking capitalism.

property-franchise.rationale: The Manifesto calls winning the battle of democracy a first step of the working class, and Marx and Lenin attacked property qualifications as bourgeois class rule.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Engels tied women's oppression to private property, but linking it to the domination of nature is an ecofeminist claim that Marxists split on.

reification.rationale: Marx's commodity fetishism, in which social relations appear as relations between things, is a core Marxist idea, though Leninist adherents give it less weight than Lukács-influenced ones.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Marxists hold that bourgeois freedoms are formal while capital owns the means of expression, and Lenin states that freedom of the press is a sham under capitalism.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Marxists see law as an instrument of class rule and the scope says Leninist and Luxemburgist strands disagree on civil liberties and legality; Lenin praised revolutionary decree and Luxemburg defended legal freedoms.

racial-franchise.rationale: Revolutionary socialism rests on class solidarity across all peoples, and the Manifesto's internationalism is incompatible with an ethnic limit on voting.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; revolutionaries stress councils and mass organisation and would not treat online deliberation as central.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from Lenin's call for officials to be elected, accountable and recallable, which implies open records; the sources do not mention publication.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Marxists regard religion as a private matter and oppose state-imposed religious restrictions on family life.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Scapegoating a religious minority divides the working class, which the family treats as the main obstacle to revolution.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: revolutionaries want class-based councils holding power, not randomly selected assemblies under bourgeois institutions; the sources do not discuss them.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Marxists criticise religion rather than reform it, but some welcome modernisation; the statement concerns religious doctrine, which the sources leave aside.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Manifesto holds that capital is a social power that dominates labour and the state, so a free society requires abolishing concentrated ownership of the means of production.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred: the tradition stands for equality against discrimination, though it said little about military service and its strands later diverged on this.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Marx and Lenin treated religion as a private matter in relation to the state, yet the Bolsheviks pursued state atheist education; the strands split.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Lenin says the bourgeois police are replaced by an armed people and coercion withers away over time, but a workers' state keeps repressive force during the transition.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The tradition frames politics around class rule by the proletarian majority, not guaranteed shares for communities; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Marx and Lenin hold that exploitation must be ended by abolishing private ownership of production, not eased by philanthropy; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution calls for officials who are elected and recallable at any time and paid workers' wages, which is compatible with limiting careers in office; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution calls for elected delegates who are recallable at any time, close to the withdrawal part of the statement; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The tradition never addressed the issue and nothing in its principles settles it.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the movement's commitment to equality between the sexes; religion itself is not its concern.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Manifesto calls for ending the bourgeois family and the subjection of women within it, so marital authority shared between equals fits the tradition.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and the Manifesto's view that workers have no country (s2); local voting rights are not discussed.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred: socialists favour restraining private rent extraction as a stop-gap, though the sources hold that reforms cannot themselves bring socialism.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's abolition of bourgeois private property in the means of production (s2); patents and copyrights are not discussed and adherents may differ on their scope.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: revolutionary socialism had its own youth leagues but not drilled national-service training; the sources do not address it.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from opposition to imperialist war and militarism (s5); nuclear basing is a later issue not covered by the sources.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialist opposition to capitalist powers' wars (s5); foreign bases are not discussed.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: revolutionary socialists condemn imperialist and colonial atrocities, but the sources do not address formal state recognition, which many see as a bourgeois-state act.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto attacks property that lives on the labour of others and the goal is an end to income from ownership of the means of production.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The sources endorse armed revolution and an armed people (s3), which is incompatible with absolute rejection of killing in defence of others.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Manifesto holds that workers have no country and that national differences are fading (s2), so essential national continuity is rejected.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and the Marxist tradition leaves this contested among adherents.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Marxist feminists are split between class-based and identity-based approaches.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Revolutionary socialists honour fallen comrades such as Luxemburg, but reject the nationalist sacralising of those who die for the nation.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Marx's materialist view treats politics as class struggle, not a spiritual contest of good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from internationalism: the sources give no homeland-diaspora doctrine, and national homelands are not a socialist aim.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: the sources make seizing political power the precondition for change (s3, s4), not cultural renewal first.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is mostly atheist and indifferent to how religion speaks of God.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: Marx treats religion as ideology to be superseded, not as a tradition to be reformed by a feminist test.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Manifesto holds that workers have no country and the economy is to be held by the working class collectively, not by a national majority.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and class-based, not ethnic, politics; the sources do not address internal borders.

independent-unions.rationale: Strands split: Luxemburgists favour mass-strike autonomy while Leninists treat unions as subordinate to the party.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Lenin and Luxemburg both make the working class's conquest of political power the core of socialism, so state ownership without it would not count.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The Manifesto's programme centralises ownership of key services in public hands, which includes basic local services.

second-chamber.rationale: Lenin praises the Commune model of a working body combining legislative and executive power in place of bourgeois parliamentary checks.

municipal-property.rationale: The Manifesto has the proletarian state centralise instruments of production, not hand them to separate communities.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Marx's Commune model is federal but Lenin stresses democratic centralism, so the strands split.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred: the Manifesto aims at abolishing wage labour, and a family wage is a reform within it.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition and no position follows from its principles.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's faith in science serving human needs under social ownership; ageing is not discussed.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; adherents want money and finance under social control but have no common view on private payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition and adherents are split between civil-liberties and security concerns.

person-over-state.rationale: The Manifesto looks to an association in which the free development of each is the condition for the free development of all.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Marx's historical materialism explains human needs and consciousness through material conditions.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The strands split between centralised state power and federal arrangements and the sources do not address regional powers.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition and no position follows from its principles.

dense-cities.rationale: The Manifesto seeks to abolish the town-country distinction, which neither endorses nor rejects density.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The tradition organises politically by class rather than race, holding that workers share interests across nations and races.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed directly; the tradition opposes racism but has no settled view on pride in ancestry.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Lenin opposes imperialist wars but backs civil war and revolutionary or national-liberation wars, so the strict defensive rule does not fit.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The Manifesto holds that workers have no country and that national differences are fading, so revolutionary socialists treat nations as secondary to class.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the class-first universalism of the Manifesto: separate religious electorates would divide workers along communal lines.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from Lenin's wartime writings, which blame imperialist rivalry and one's own ruling class rather than a plot against the nation.

free-public-college.rationale: The Manifesto's programme demands free public education; extending that to colleges is inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: revolutionary socialists would favour abolishing private production for profit and planning it, not pricing pollution within capitalism, which they hold cannot be reformed.

future-generations.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; Marx's critique of capital's exhaustion of soil and labour (s6) suggests mild agreement.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: the tradition frames women's emancipation through class struggle and equal participation, not as bringing distinct values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Wartime writings oppose imperialist war but the tradition also arms the revolution and rejects pacifism, so adherents are split.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Lenin's wartime writings denounce the imperialist powers' secret dealings; open diplomacy is inferred as the socialist alternative.

capital-controls.rationale: The Manifesto calls for centralising credit in the hands of the state, which implies control over capital flows.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Revolutionary socialists hold that a workers' state needs armed force and want an armed people, so a state monopoly is contested between militia and standing-army views; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Lenin states a revolutionary class cannot but desire its own government's defeat in a reactionary war and urges soldiers to turn the war into a civil war.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The movement backs unions as schools of class struggle and collective action, though it sees bargaining within capitalism as insufficient.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credits are a reform within capitalism that revolutionary socialists neither champion nor oppose in principle; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Revolutionary socialists reject constraints on state spending under capitalism and see fiscal rules as bourgeois orthodoxy; inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The movement is anti-imperialist and wants an end to the exploitation of poorer countries, but it seeks to replace the capitalist order, not only reform its rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution argues that the proletariat must smash the bourgeois state machine, not take it over.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Marxists reject utopian blueprints, but revolutionary socialists want a single socialist economy in common ownership, not coexisting market systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Marxist theory ties value to labour, not nature, and reads pricing nature as capital as a capitalist logic; the sources do not discuss it, so inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country and the movement is internationalist, rejecting the sacralised nation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Revolutionary socialists support relief for workers burdened by debt as a gain for the working class; inferred, as the sources do not mention student loans.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Lenin and Marxist analysis of imperialism describe core regions draining peripheries, and an internal version is a natural extension; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Marx held that human nature is historically shaped by social relations, so it is not a fixed basis to be left unchanged.

public-service-media.rationale: Revolutionary socialists want public media free of capital but doubt that any state under capitalism is independent of it; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Marx's critique of religion treats it as a product of social conditions, and the Manifesto and later Marxists reject religious worldviews, so claims of one underlying spiritual truth are not accepted.

farm-price-support.rationale: Revolutionary socialists back peasant and farm-worker demands within the fight against capital, though they aim at socialised agriculture rather than price supports; inferred as mild support.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Revolutionary socialists oppose imperialist rivalries and militarism and want disarmament of the bourgeois state, though Lenin and later workers' states built nuclear weapons; inferred as mild disagreement for the doctrine.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Manifesto says communists form a distinct party opposed to other working-class parties and the established ones, and Luxemburg and Lenin both treat an independent working-class party as the means of conquering power.

ban-fgm.rationale: Revolutionary socialists support equal rights for women and the Manifesto calls for the abolition of the bourgeois family; FGM is not addressed so a ban is inferred as mild agreement, with some strands wary of state prohibition.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Manifesto's programme includes abolishing inheritance rights of private property and equality of women is a long-standing socialist demand; equal rights to own and inherit land for women follows from this.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Revolutionary socialism has no doctrine about language classification; the issue lies outside the ideology.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Revolutionary socialists want social ownership of production and public planning, and see liability suits between private owners as a bourgeois frame; they favour collective control over pollution, inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The Manifesto and State and Revolution reject hereditary and privileged authorities and want the state replaced by workers' self-rule, so an official role for chiefs in lawmaking is opposed.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Revolutionary socialists criticise capitalism's destruction of nature, but the doctrine does not rank the environment against liberty; strands differ, so neutral.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Revolutionary socialists see criminal law as class rule and want it reshaped by workers' power; fixed sentences are not a priority and are inferred as mildly opposed, though strands differ.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The Manifesto holds that workers have no country and the movement is internationalist, so compulsory language tests for immigrants are inferred as mildly opposed.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Revolutionary socialists want strong, class-wide unions, and closed-shop arrangements are common in their tradition; inferred, not stated in the sources.

voter-id.rationale: They see bourgeois elections as a class instrument and would oppose barriers that exclude workers, but the issue is peripheral; inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Their tradition treats religion as a private matter and rejects any state church; inferred from that secular-state principle.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Lenin and Luxemburg describe bourgeois democracy as class rule and require real working-class power beyond elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: The Manifesto attacks bourgeois marriage and the family, though later Leninist strands were split on sexual morality; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: They oppose censorship by the capitalist state, though a revolutionary state might curb counter-revolution; inferred and contested.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Replacing welfare with a cash payment preserves wage labour and markets, which they seek to abolish; inferred from core principles.

women-suffrage.rationale: Socialist movements of the Second and Third Internationals demanded equal political rights for women; inferred from the tradition.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Marx and Engels trace women's subordination mainly to property and class society rather than religion; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: The tradition treats race as a tool of class division, but the foundational texts do not discuss it directly; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: They distrust bourgeois state machinery as a vehicle of liberation, favouring working-class self-organisation; inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto's central demand is abolishing bourgeois property in the means of production, so first-claim ownership of resources is rejected.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the view that state and law serve class rule; courts above nations would be seen as instruments of imperial powers, and the sources do not address them.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Marx treated religion as the opium of the people and a product of alienation, so literal scriptural authority is rejected.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's call for equality and ending women's treatment as instruments of production; the sources do not discuss self-government arrangements.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Strands split: Trotskyists defend a degenerated workers' state unconditionally, while Luxemburgist and other currents refuse to defend a bureaucratic regime.

indirect-election.rationale: Strands split: Lenin favoured a pyramid of soviets with recallable delegates, while the Commune model and Luxemburg stressed direct, mass democracy.

national-church-status.rationale: The Manifesto and Marxist tradition treat religion as bourgeois ideology, and Lenin's programme separated church from state, so no church gets special legal status.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from Lenin's support for national self-determination and regional autonomy, though Luxemburg opposed national autonomy, so strands are split.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from Lenin's support for self-determination of nations; the sources do not address plebiscites directly.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from internationalism, which sees borders as bourgeois constructs; the sources do not address colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: The formula 'from each according to his needs' presupposes abundance, so socialism aims at plenty rather than limited wants.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents have no settled position on settlement limits in indigenous homelands.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the call for the armed people and the equal status of women in the proletariat; the sources do not discuss conscription of women.

missingStatements.text: The working class should take power through its own councils, with the old police and bureaucracy replaced by an armed people.
missingStatements.rationale: Lenin's State and Revolution demands breaking the bourgeois state machine and replacing it with an armed people organised in a militia.

missingStatements.text: Reforms won within capitalism cannot by themselves bring about socialism; a seizure of political power by the working class is required.
missingStatements.rationale: Luxemburg argues reforms operate only within the framework of the last revolution, and that conquest of political power is the proletariat's necessary aim.

missingStatements.text: Socialists should oppose their own country's war effort in a war between capitalist powers.
missingStatements.rationale: Lenin states a revolutionary class cannot but desire its own government's defeat in a reactionary war, and the 1914 split turned on this question.

notes: Leninist and Luxemburgist strands split on vanguard party, one-party rule, emergency measures and civil liberties, so those are 0 or low. Many modern-issue answers are inferred from the tradition's principles.
